property_summary: After any operation, the supportsInterface function must return true for both IAccessControl and IERC165 interface IDs.
After any cancel operation, the result of supportsInterface for the IERC165 interface ID must be the same as before the cancel operation.
The supportsInterface function must return true for the IERC165 interface ID after any cancel operation.
For any bytes4 selector s, if c.supportsInterface(s) returns true for 4 distinct values of s, then s must include both type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and type(IERC165).interfaceId.
After any cancel operation, the contract's supportsInterface returns true for the IERC165 interface ID.
The cancel function should revert when called with an operation id that is not pending.
hasRole returns true for the contract itself with TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE after deployment.
Calling cancel on a non-pending operation should revert because hasRole returns false for PROPOSER_ROLE, making the onlyRole modifier revert.

The `cancel` function reverts when called with a random `bytes32` id because the caller does not have PROPOSER_ROLE, but in the mutated version it does not revert because the `onlyRole` modifier no longer checks the role correctly.
A cancel call on a pending operation always succeeds for the caller who has PROPOSER_ROLE.
The cancel function reverts when called with a non-pending operation id.
After canceling an operation, it becomes non-pending (isOperationPending returns false).
For any operation id, after calling cancel(id), if the caller does not have the PROPOSER_ROLE then cancel reverts.
hasRole returns true for any role and account.
For any role and account, if hasRole returns true for the zero address then cancel with id keccak256(abi.encode(params)) can be called without PROPOSER_ROLE, else it reverts.
For any role, getRoleAdmin returns the same role as adminRole (self-admin) for TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE, or TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE for PROPOSER/EXECUTOR roles; the buggy version always returns 0x00.
After a successful cancel, the operation's timestamp remains 0, meaning isOperation returns false.
After a successful cancel of a pending operation by a proposer, the operation's timestamp is zero, and getRoleAdmin returns the admin role of the role used to authorize the cancel.
For any role, the admin role returned by getRoleAdmin must be either TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE (0x00 for DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, but the buggy version breaks by always returning 0x00).
After canceling an operation, getRoleAdmin returns the same admin role as before the cancel, but the mutant always returns 0x00.

After a cancel operation, the operation's timestamp is either zero (if it was pending) or remains unchanged (if it was not pending), but it never becomes the DONE_TIMESTAMP (1) unless it was already ready.
After a cancel operation, the operation's timestamp is either zero (if it was pending) or unchanged (if it was not pending), but never becomes the DONE_TIMESTAMP (1).
After any cancel, the operation timestamp is either unchanged or zero, never set to DONE_TIMESTAMP (1) unless it was already ready and then executed.
After canceling an operation that is pending, its timestamp is set to zero (not the DONE_TIMESTAMP).
After cancel, the operation timestamp is either zero or unchanged, never set to DONE_TIMESTAMP (1).
After scheduling and then cancelling an operation, calling renounceRole on any account other than self should fail in the reference but succeed in the mutant.
After scheduling and then cancelling an operation, calling renounceRole on an account other than self reverts in the reference but succeeds in the mutant.

After a successful cancel of a pending operation, the sender (who holds the PROPOSER_ROLE) retains the ability to revoke their own role via renounceRole, but in the broken version renounceRole always reverts.
After canceling a pending operation, an account other than msg.sender can still renounce its own role in the reference but not in the broken version.
After calling cancel, the sender address can always renounce its own role (PROPOSER_ROLE) without reverting.
After any operation, renouncing a role for self must revoke not grant the role
The caller's role is not granted after calling cancel.
After any call to cancel, the caller never has the PROPOSER_ROLE granted to them.
After canceling an operation, the caller's PROPOSER_ROLE membership is unchanged (never granted).
After a user renounces their own PROPOSER_ROLE, they no longer have that role.

For any operation id, the return value of isOperation(id) should be consistent with the return value of isOperationPending(id): if isOperation(id) is true then isOperationPending(id) must also be true, because the only way to set a timestamp to a non-zero value is to schedule the operation (setting timestamp > 1) and cancel only sets it to 0, so getTimestamp(id) > 0 is equivalent to getTimestamp(id) >= 2, while getTimestamp(id) != 0 also could be true if getTimestamp(id) == 1 (i.e., operation done), but then isOperationPending would be false since isOperationPending requires > 1.
After cancellation, an operation should not be marked as pending.
For any bytes32 id, if c.isOperation(id) returns false, then c.isOperationPending(id) must also return false.
After canceling an operation, isOperation must return false.
For all operations, isOperation(id) is true if and only if isOperationPending(id) is true.
After a new operation is successfully scheduled, calling cancel with that operation's id must not revert and must mark the operation as no longer pending.
Cancelling an operation that is already completed should revert.
Cancelling an operation that is not yet pending (getTimestamp returns 0) should always revert.
Cancelling an operation that has a timestamp equal to _DONE_TIMESTAMP (i.e., already executed) always reverts.
Cancelling an operation that has a timestamp greater than _DONE_TIMESTAMP (i.e., is pending and not yet executed) should not revert if called by a proposer.
For any id, after cancel(id) reverts, the operation is not pending (getTimestamp(id) == 0).
For any id, calling cancel(id) when isOperation(id) is false reverts.
Before cancel(id), checking the operation status (isOperation) must reflect the schedule state; if the operation was never scheduled, isOperation is false.
If cancel id returns true, then the operation was pending before the call.
For any id, if cancel(id) does not revert, then after the call, isOperation(id) returns false.
Cancel should only be possible for pending operations (isOperation(id) must return true).
After canceling an operation, the operation should not be pending.
After executing a scheduled operation, the operation's timestamp should equal DONE_TIMESTAMP (1).
For any operation id, isOperation(id) must be false when getTimestamp(id) equals 0.
isOperation returns false when getTimestamp returns 0 for any operation id.
The `isOperation` function returns true for any operation that has been scheduled (i.e., has a non-zero timestamp).
For any operation id, cancel(bytes32) reverts if and only if isOperation(id) is false
For any operation id, after calling cancel(id), the operation is no longer pending (isOperationPending returns false).
Cancel reverts if and only if isOperation returns true (i.e., operation exists) and isOperationPending returns true (i.e., operation is not done).
For any operation id, cancel(id) succeeds if and only if isOperation(id) is true and isOperationPending(id) is true.
isOperation(id) returns true if and only if the operation's timestamp is not 0.
If cancel(id) succeeds, then the timestamp of that operation is set to 1 (DONE_TIMESTAMP).
If an operation is not pending (isOperationPending returns false), then cancel should revert.
After a successful call to cancel(id), isOperation(id) returns false (i.e., the timestamp is 0, not 1).
After calling cancel(id), isOperation returns false if and only if the operation was pending (had a timestamp > 1).

The isOperation function should return true exactly when getTimestamp(id) > 0, not when getTimestamp(id) > 1, and this can be tested by ensuring that a newly scheduled operation (with a known timestamp > 0) returns true for isOperation.
After scheduling an operation, calling cancel on it must make isOperation return false.
The cancel function should revert when called on an operation that is not pending (isOperationPending returns false).
After scheduling an operation, the operation's id must be considered pending until cancelled.
An operation is considered pending iff its timestamp is greater than 1.
For any operation id, isOperation(id) returns false if and only if cancel(id) will revert.
If an operation is pending (isOperationPending returns true), then calling cancel(id) must not revert.
For any operation id, isOperation(id) returns true if and only if getTimestamp(id) > 0.
If an operation is cancelled, then isOperation(id) must return false.
Calling isOperation on a scheduled operation returns true before cancellation and false after cancellation, but the mutant isOperation always returns false.
For any operation, isOperationPending returns false for timestamps equal to _DONE_TIMESTAMP.
After calling cancel on a pending operation, isOperationPending returns false for that operation.
A cancelled operation that was pending must not be done.
If isOperationDone returns true for an operation, then isOperationPending must return false for that same operation.
After a cancel operation reverts, the operation's isOperationPending status remains unchanged from before the cancel attempt.
isOperationPending returns false only when getTimestamp returns exactly 1 (DONE_TIMESTAMP).
After cancel, isOperationPending returns false for the canceled operation id.
isOperationPending returns false after cancel returns true.
When cancel(bytes32) is called on an operation that is both pending and ready, the operation should become not pending after the cancellation.
If isOperationPending returns true for an id, then getTimestamp(id) must be greater than 1.
If an operation is not pending, then cancel should revert.
Cancelling a non-pending operation always reverts.

Cancelling an operation successfully requires that isOperationPending returns true for that operation's id, so if cancel does not revert then isOperationPending must have returned true before the call.
Before cancel succeeds, isOperationPending must return true for the id derived from the operation that was scheduled.
If cancel does not revert, then isOperationPending must have returned true for that id before the call.

For any operation id, if isOperationReady(id) returns true, then the operation should be ready on or after the current block timestamp, but the buggy version only considers operations ready strictly before the current timestamp.
If cancel is called on a ready operation, it should revert because the operation can only be cancelled when pending, not when ready.
If cancel is called on an operation that is ready, it should revert.
The isOperationReady function returns true for operations whose timestamp equals the current block timestamp.
If operation is ready (isOperationReady returns true), then cancel should revert because only pending operations can be cancelled.
